newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT - Ill Lomu may play most NPC games.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Ill Lomu may play most NPC games.

text.p: WELLINGTON, June 13 - Star All Black rugby winger Jonah Lomu could be playing again within three months, NZPA reported on Friday.
Lomu's treatment for a serious kidney disease is going so well he could play most of the national championship season for Counties-Manukau.
That is the best-case scenario painted by All Black doctor John Mayhew, who is overseeing Lomu's drug treatment for nephrotic syndrome.
Lomu is overseas, where he has been watching the French Tennis Open and visiting South Africa. The break coincides with a quiet part of his treatment.
"He's in the second-to-last month of his treatment options, six or seven weeks to go. But we won't know until the treatment has finished how successful it will be.
"But he's been pretty compliant with the treatment. It's been pretty unpleasant stuff.
"It consists of alternate months of different drugs. Every alternate month he has three days of intravenous medication, and that makes him feel washed out for a few days.
"But physically he's handled it well and psychologically he's been an eye-opener. He's been good."
Mayhew said statistics give Lomu just a 50 percent chance of being cured -- "it's not definite, but he's doing everything he can possibly do".
There's no rushing the treatment and tests, but on an optimistic note, Mayhew says things are looking positive.
Lomu is on a gentle fitness programme, doing gym work when he can, cycling and playing golf.
"We're worried that on the drug programme he's on that the steroids could damage his joints if he did a lot of running," Mayhew said.
"He looks in good shape, but we'll only know when we get him off the treatment and back into training. The best possible scenario is that he could play the NPC, from the start."
Meanwhile, Lomu's sickness claim against his insurance company is "substantial", his lawyer said.
"It is certainly a lot of money," Paul Dale, of Grove Darlow and Partners, said after a hearing before Master Kennedy Grant in the High Court in Auckland yesterday.

His lawyers issued summary judgment proceedings against GIO Insurance, which specialises in insuring sports people in New Zealand, Australia and elsewhere, after the company rejected Lomu's claim for sickness insurance.
After yesterday's hearing, neither GIO Insurance nor Dale would specify the amount claimed because it would indicate Lomu's earnings.
